newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bankgesellschaft - no reason to doubt merger.
newsitem.headline: Bankgesellschaft - no reason to doubt merger.

text.p: Germany's Bankgesellschaft Berlin AG said on Monday its merger talks with Norddeutsche Landesbank (NordLB) were proceeding according to plan and that there was no reason to doubt that the fusion would go ahead.
"There is no need to cast doubt on the merger project," a Bankgesellschaft spokeswoman said.

News magazine Der Spiegel reported on Monday the chances of a merger had deteriorated because Bankgesellschaft was disappointed at the first valuation of the two banks and because of differences about the name of the new bank and representation on its supervisory board.
Bankgesellschaft and regional bank Norddeutsche Landesbank, both state-owned banks, said in May they were beginning merger talks to create one of the country's largest banking groups.

The banks said a working party of management and their federal state owners had proposed fusing NordLB into a group led by Bankgesellschaft as early as mid-1998, pending talks due for completion this year.
Bankgesellshaft is currently 56 percent owned by the city state of Berlin while NordLB is owned by three different federal states, mainly Lower Saxony.
The Spiegel report said Bankgesellschaft had been disappointed at the valuation which revealed weaknesses in NordLB's investment banking business.
